top_choice_rationale: Mircea Cărtărescu alone (P001) is the only writer on the slate, and on the common criteria he is the best-supported choice. From public knowledge of Blinding (the Orbitor sequence) and Solenoid, his voice is distinctive. His formal achievement lies in building very large, patterned structures in which memory, the body and dream form one metaphysical project. The oeuvre looks consolidated, so I see no timing problem. The citation should rest on the prose and name poetry only as a root, since translated coverage of the poetry is thin. Key uncertainties remain. I judge the Romanian prose only through translation. I cannot settle whether the late novels deepen their image systems or recirculate them. The poetry-as-root claim is a hypothesis. These are limits of access, not findings against the work. They do not justify no award, so P000 ranks last. The unanimous opening support is not treated as merit. I have not read the corpus for this exercise or independently verified any source.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. Documented connections are collegial: election in the 2019 renewal round with Ellen Mattson, and service with Olsson, Mattson, Sem-Sandberg and Palm. I have publicly said the Academy has overlooked many significant women's authorships, but I do not use gender, nationality or language as a criterion of merit here. This is disclosed and not adjudicated.
